title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Study, Publicity, and Implementation of the Adoption Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Adoption Law of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [1992] No. 11

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

The Adoption Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Adoption Law) was adopted by the 23rd Session of the Standing Committee of the Seventh National People's Congress and shall come into force on April 1, 1992. The Adoption Law serves as the standard for citizens in handling adoption matters and as the basis for people's courts in correctly adjudicating adoption cases. In order to correctly implement the Adoption Law, the following notice is hereby given:

I. People's courts at all levels shall organize cadres and police officers to earnestly study the Adoption Law, grasp its legislative intent, and in light of local conditions, closely cooperate with relevant departments to carry out extensive, in-depth publicity activities, so that the broad masses of the people can understand and comply with the Adoption Law, enhance citizens' legal awareness, and properly handle adoption matters.

II. After the Adoption Law comes into force, people's courts at all levels must strictly implement it. For adoption relationships established after the Adoption Law comes into force, the Adoption Law shall apply when adjudicating them. For adoption cases accepted before the Adoption Law comes into force but not yet concluded by the time it takes effect, or for adoption relationships established before the Adoption Law comes into force where parties subsequently file a lawsuit to confirm the adoption relationship after the Adoption Law comes into force, the relevant provisions in effect at the time shall apply when adjudicating; if no provisions existed at that time, the matter may be handled by reference to the Adoption Law. For adoption relationships established before the Adoption Law comes into force, if parties subsequently file a lawsuit to dissolve the adoption relationship after the Adoption Law comes into force, the Adoption Law shall apply.

III. For adoption cases that were concluded by people's courts before the Adoption Law came into force, if parties apply for a retrial or a retrial is conducted under the trial supervision procedure after the Adoption Law comes into force, the relevant provisions in effect at the time of the original conclusion shall apply.

IV. Any provisions or interpretations made by the Supreme People's Court on adoption matters before the Adoption Law came into force that contravene the Adoption Law shall no longer apply from now on.

V. In the process of implementing the Adoption Law, people's courts at all levels shall strengthen investigation and research, promptly summarize experiences regarding new situations and problems arising in adoption cases, and collect and compile typical cases to report to this Court for timely research and summarization.

March 26, 1992
